slot.brief: Unpolarized light reflected off a glass surface; use Brewster's law to identify the angle at which reflected light becomes polarized, given refractive index.

stem: An unpolarized light beam in air is incident on the surface of a glass plate of refractive index $\mu = \sqrt{3}$. The angle of incidence at which the reflected light is completely plane-polarized is:

verdicts.working: Reflected light is fully plane-polarized at Brewster's angle: tan θ_B = μ = √3, so θ_B = 60°.

working:
According to Brewster's law, when light is incident at Brewster's angle ($i_p$), the reflected beam is completely polarized:
$$\tan i_p = \mu$$
Given $\mu = \sqrt{3}$:
$$\tan i_p = \sqrt{3} \implies i_p = 60^\circ$$

Independent check: Reflected light is fully plane-polarized at Brewster's angle: tan θ_B = μ = √3, so θ_B = 60°.

draft.distractor_notes:
$30^\circ$ corresponds to the angle of refraction ($r = 90^\circ - i_p$) or confusing $\tan 30^\circ$ with $\tan 60^\circ$.
$45^\circ$ comes from assuming $\mu = 1$ in Brewster's condition.
